_comment: WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT CODE (OR A CLAUDE.md RULE):
How a board LOOKS is a product decision that will be re-tuned many times,
by people who are not editing Python. Keeping it as data means the look can
change without touching the renderer, two looks can be compared by swapping
one argument, and the chosen preset ships with the product instead of living
'clean' is the house style used for PIPELINE diagrams (extraction/retrieval
journeys): straight edges, Nunito, maximum legibility in a paper.
'graphic-recording' is the opposite on purpose - sketchy edges, hand-drawn
font, size hierarchy - because a graphic recording is a POSTER, not a
diagram. Same renderer, different data. The repo uses 'clean' everywhere

clean.description: House style for pipeline diagrams. Maximum legibility.

graphic-recording._why_roughness: 1 is Excalidraw's hand-drawn stroke. It is deliberately OFF for pipeline diagrams (harder to read at figure size) and deliberately ON here, because the marker look is what makes a board read as a graphic recording rather than a spreadsheet.
graphic-recording._why_font: 5 = Excalifont, Excalidraw's hand-drawn face. Legibility is worse than Nunito, which is why the pipeline diagrams do not use it. On a poster it is the point. Swap to 6 if it proves unreadable at presentation size - that is exactly the kind of change this file exists to make cheap.
graphic-recording._why_header: Headline words are hand-lettered and LARGE. On a real board five to eight big words carry the whole structure; everything else is subordinate.
graphic-recording._why_card_sizes: Size hierarchy is the main signal a graphic recording uses. A live decision is drawn big; something the meeting has moved past is small and faded. Uniform cards are what makes our current board look like a Kanban wall.
graphic-recording._why_shape: Ellipses read as hand-drawn blobs and break the grid. Rectangles read as a table.
graphic-recording._why_icons: Pictograms are half of what makes a board legible at a glance. These are text glyphs for now - a placeholder for real shapes pulled from an .excalidrawlib (libraries.excalidraw.com, MIT, and just JSON element groups we can inject).
